title: 7th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran 9:01 to 10:32 under the Speaker. A written question on the delayed cath lab at Addu Equatorial Hospital was answered by the Health Minister, then MPs voted 45-1 to debate an urgent motion from South Galolhu MP Meekail Ahmed Nasym asking the government to prepare for the effects of the Middle East war on tourism, fuel, medicine and food stocks. Government-side and opposition MPs debated it until time ran out, trading arguments about reserves, debt and past governments. Debate then began on the government's bill to amend the Thalassemia Control Act (Act 2012/4) but was left open for the next sitting. Parts of the text layer are garbled, so the attendance labels are a best reading.

items.title: Opening of the sitting
items.outcome: Speaker opened the sitting with prayers

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 39 members present, 2 on leave, 1 on official travel (best reading)

items.title: Urgent motion on preparing for the effects of the Middle East war on the Maldives
items.outcome: Voted 45-1 to debate; debated by 15 members until time ran out

items.title: Written question to the Health Minister on the cath lab at Addu Equatorial Hospital
items.outcome: Question asked by Central Hithadhoo MP; minister's written answer tabled

items.title: Preliminary debate on the government bill to amend the Thalassemia Control Act (Act 2012/4)
items.outcome: Introduced and debated by 4 members; debate left open for the next sitting

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the usable reserve is mostly borrowed money, including a USD 400 million India currency swap, and questioned funds for fuel and imports.
Said state debt rose from MVR 120 billion in 2023 to 144.5 billion at end 2024, and that businesses face a dollar shortage.
Said development projects have stalled, citing about 12 percent of the MVR 12.3 billion development budget spent.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Moved the urgent motion asking the government to prepare for war-related effects on tourism, fuel, gas, medicine and food stocks.
Asked for assurance on essential stocks, dollar reserves and honest public finance figures, and framed it as non-partisan.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Raised a point of order that the Finance Ministry publishes reserves weekly, latest about USD 850 million, calling other figures misinformation.
On the thalassemia bill, fully supported it and asked for pre-marriage genetic testing under Aasandha and support for affected children.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Condemned Israel's attack on Iran and warned of oil supply risk if the Strait of Hormuz is closed, urging special rules.
Said the government paid over MVR 1.3 billion in debt this month, questioned the MDP's motive, played an audio clip, and credited the president for the Israeli passport ban.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Said the MDP supports the concern, warning of effects on oil, the dollar rate above MVR 19 and tourist arrivals via Gulf hubs.
Said the MDP's video showed it wanting peace and offered opposition support to the government.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked why the cath lab at Addu Equatorial Hospital is delayed and when its service will start.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the government is acting openly on essential supplies, stood with Palestinians and Iranians, and compared past governments' handling of crises.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the motion is worth debating, cited MVR 128 billion in debt left by the previous government, and urged opposition parties to back the president's policy.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said ministers are already working on the war's effects and criticised the MDP's past tourism boycott actions.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Thanked the mover, condemned Israel's actions, and called for the government to consult the tourism industry and opposition and secure essential stocks.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Agreed the issue merits debate, said the government is already acting, and accused the opposition of politicising tourism concerns; defended current finances.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Thanked the mover, expressed confidence in the president's response, condemned Israel, and urged reform and self-reliance, including for the nation's youth.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Thanked the mover, argued the government is prepared and acting on the war, including the Israeli passport ban, and disputed MDP claims on debt.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the government is doing all it can, blamed the debt on loans taken by the MDP government, and condemned Israeli attacks.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said ministers are already acting and the Israeli passport ban stands; criticised the MDP's Covid ventilator purchases and said debt is about 124 percent of GDP.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said the motion aims to harm the economy, and that the president has cut debt without printing money, citing a recorded MVR 1.5 billion surplus.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Introduced the bill: sets rules for the Thalassemia Centre's director general and for marriage of likely carriers, amending Act 2012/4 for the first time in 13 years.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the amendment, said thalassemia is common in the Maldives, and urged more public and school awareness to lower its rate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Welcomed the amendment and said island hospitals lack thalassemia centres and proper services for affected children.

decisions: The Majlis voted 45-1 to take up the urgent motion on preparing for the war's effects, with 24 votes needed.
Debate on the urgent motion ended when its allotted time ran out; no further vote on it is recorded in this part.
The Health Minister's written answer on the Addu Equatorial Hospital cath lab was tabled: works about 98 percent done, an operator being sought, service expected in about four months.
Debate on the thalassemia bill was left open to continue at the next sitting on Wednesday 25 June 2025 at 9:00.
